rrc.format: One PDF per calendar year of new construction reports (Form PS-48), 2008 to 2026. Not a T-4 permit dataset. Parsed here with pdftotext. Separate: RRC publishes 'Pipeline Layers by County' shapefiles (255 county zips, about 182 MB for the first 250, updated twice a week, via a GoAnywhere file-transfer page that needs a browser click-through) which carry the T-4 permit number per line but no permit issue date. No bulk T-4 permit table exists; RRC says permits filed since 2015 live only in its POPS system and older permits are searchable one at a time as PDFs.
rrc.fields: PS-48 PDFs: received date, report number (e.g. 25-NC-078), notification ID, operator, system ID, system name, T-4 permit number (placeholder 12345, 01234 or 55555 means not yet permitted or not yet added to an existing permit; 99999 distribution; 66666 breakout tank), start date, county, RRC region, product type (natural gas gathering / transmission / distribution, hazardous liquid, crude), miles, diameter, and (2025 on) new system vs extension. Shapefiles (per Harris County mirror of RRC data): operator, system name, T4PERMIT, diameter, commodity, interstate flag, status, county, length. Neither says new vs amended permit directly; the PS-48 'new system' vs 'extension' flag is the nearest.

new_permits_by_year.note: These are new construction reports, not issued T-4 permits. PS-48 covers transmission, gathering in Class 2/3/4 locations, and some distribution, so rural gathering is undercounted. 2026 runs to Sept 18 only. Counts come from my own regex parse of the PDFs; 2023 has 2 and 2024 has 1 unparseable rows.

rrc.count_method: I downloaded the RRC's four yearly new-construction-report PDFs for 2023 to 2026, converted them to text, and counted rows by product type, system type, and miles (25 km is 15.5 miles). I did not find any RRC dataset that counts T-4 permits themselves by year, so the per-year numbers are construction reports, a proxy. Note the RRC labels many large Permian lines 'natural gas transmission' even when they are gathering-like, so the 25 km count (6 to 16 a year) is an upper bound for what GGIT would add from Texas intrastate. No dates or counts of actual T-4 issuance were found; I did not download the 182 MB county shapefiles because they carry no permit date.

taps_estimate: Confirmed: one data-center prior-notice filing, Transwestern's Green Chile lateral (CP26-80), and it is a lateral and meter station that is stalled by land and environmental review, not a simple tap. I pulled all 186 Federal Register 'Notice of Request Under Blanket Authorization' notices published since 2024-01-01 and searched their text: only that one says data center. Six more serve new gas power plants or power generation (Enable, Transco twice, El Paso, Gulf South, NGPL) with no stated data-center link. Self-implementing (automatic authorization) filings are not published in the Federal Register and I could not search FERC eLibrary, so those are uncounted. My estimate is that explicit data-center taps under blanket authority are very few, probably fewer than 10 since 2024 and likely 1 to 5 by what filings say, but I am not sure, because pipelines often name only the customer (for example a utility or a developer LLC) and not the end use. Several named pipelines (Texas Eastern, Tennessee Gas, Columbia, Rockies Express, Northern Natural, Southern Natural, Texas Gas, Equitrans) showed no data-center prior notice in the Federal Register scan, but customer names were not checked against data-center developers.
not_found: No bulk dataset of T-4 permits with issue dates or new vs amended flags; no RRC count of T-4 permits per year; no RRC page or news item naming a T-4 permit for a data center (the data-center links above come from operator names in construction reports plus news context, and none is source-confirmed except Abilene DC 1, LLC's operator name). I did not download the 182 MB county shapefiles (they lack permit dates and need a browser click-through). No FERC automatic-authorization filings were searched, since FERC eLibrary is not scriptable with curl. I did not read each Federal Register power-plant notice fully for customer names that might be data-center developers. Four web searches for Texas Eastern, Transco, Tennessee, Columbia and Northern Natural data-center taps returned only operational notices. No Energy Transfer or Abilene source I fetched ties the Stargate Pipeline 24in report to the campus directly. Some per-year counts come from a regex over PDF text and could be off by a few rows.
